filed_by: hand-filed with the fix for issue #57
diff_then: stdout: 'nested => "[\"a\", [\"b\", [\"c\"]]]"' vs 'nested => "a/b/c"'; 'a/ then /b => "a///b"' vs '"a/b"'; a self-containing array ran to the fuel limit instead of raising
note: `File.join` was `parts.map { |x| x.to_s }.join("/")`, which is not `rb_file_join`: a nested Array was rendered with `Array#to_s` instead of joined first, a separator run was doubled (`File.join("a/", "/b")` answered `"a///b"`), and an array containing itself lost the whole program to the fuel limit instead of raising `ArgumentError: recursive array`. The prelude now walks CRuby's loop: each element is a path (`FilePathStringValue`) or a joined Array, the array being joined and its ancestors are the cycle test, an element starting with `/` replaces the collected separators and one that does not gets a `/` only when the result does not already end with one. Found while fixing the coercion half (`File.join(1, 2)`), which is the same call site.
